sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter is called (i lunga) /i ˈluŋɡo/. Its main sound appears in (jeans) /dʒins/, which means denim trousers. The letter has two sounds in Italian words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, press your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Stop the air, then push your lips forward as the air bursts through. Next, raise the middle of your tongue close to the hard roof. Keep your lips relaxed and let the air flow smoothly. Put a hand on your throat. Your vocal cords shake for both sounds.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: In English loanwords, say it like the start of (jeans) /dʒins/. In older Italian words, names, or Latin borrowings, say it like (juventino) /juvenˈtino/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the gliding sound into the sound in English jam. In older names, keep the air smooth without a burst. Just raise the tongue like the y in English yes.
